name: Quadrantids
notes: Sharp peak ~6h. Cold-weather shower. Radiant in northern Boötes.

name: Lyrids
notes: Bright meteors, occasional fireballs. Radiant near Vega.

name: Eta Aquariids
notes: Halley's Comet debris. Best pre-dawn. Better seen from southern hemisphere.

name: Southern δ Aquariids
notes: Steady rate over many nights, no sharp peak.

name: Perseids
notes: Most reliable summer shower. Comet Swift-Tuttle. Best for photography.

name: Draconids
notes: Slow meteors. Can outburst unpredictably. Evening shower.

name: Orionids
notes: Halley's Comet debris (second). Fast and faint.

name: Leonids
notes: 33-year cycle: storm years (~1999) produce thousands; off years ~15.

name: Geminids
notes: Strongest annual shower. Slow, bright multi-colored meteors. Asteroid 3200 Phaethon.

name: Ursids
notes: Circumpolar from N hemisphere — visible all night.
